 Nations Championship England v Japan: Nations Championship rugby union – live
 Updates from 4.40pm (GMT) start at the Allianz Stadium
 Report: Wales stun New Zealand | Email Alex

 1m ago 13.26 EST 78 min: Japan showed flickers of life earlier this half, but it’s all England now – their replacements have been just as ruthless as the starting XV. The visitors have the ball now though (as Opeti Helu limps off) – it’s their lineout.
 Share 4m ago 13.23 EST 75 min: Will Joseph is named man of the match – surprise, surprise. He’s scored five of England’s 13 tries. Unlucky for Japan.
 Share 6m ago 13.22 EST TRY! England 78-15 Japan (Fisilau)
 Greg Fisilau apparently got the ball down after England mauled for the line. They’re off target from the tee once again. Another miss; all the home fans in Twickenham are delighted while Jonny Wilkinson is at home nobly weeping.
 Share 9m ago 13.19 EST 72 min: Samisoni Tua is off for head injury check but appears OK. Mercilessly, England power towards Japan’s try-line … the TMO is checking whether the hosts got the ball down.
 Share 12m ago 13.16 EST 71 min: Greg Fisilau thumps into a Japan player – Samisoni Tua, I think, who is whacked to the deck. I can’t quite see as he’s immediately getting some treatment. Thankfully, he’s up and looks OK. Some carry from Fisilau.
 Share 14m ago 13.14 EST 70 min: England once again flying up their right flank – but this time Japan stop them. Apparently this is the most points England have scored at Twickenham in 25 years. Theo Dan gets some treatment on his shoulder after a meaty tackle. England’s lineout.
 Share 16m ago 13.12 EST TRY! England 73-15 Japan (Smith)
 England spread the ball about – Ojomoh and McParland involved – Marcus Smith with some fancy footwork and he adds his name to the try-scorers list. Phew!
 View image in fullscreen England's Marcus Smith makes it twelve. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA Share Updated at  13.20 EST 17m ago 13.10 EST 66 min: England’s scrum, they get the ball out wide – looking for Joseph once again. McParland is getting involved now, showing his skills. They’re right on Japan’s try-line.
 Share 19m ago 13.08 EST TRY! England 66-15 Japan (Curry)
 An 11th England try – Ben Curry with his first try for his country. Just exploiting the space in the Japan defence as he picks up and cruises over. Henry Slade misses the conversion – the hosts have only converted three times from 11.
 View image in fullscreen England's Ben Curry looks up as he celebrates after scoring a try. Photograph: Kin Cheung/AP Share Updated at  13.19 EST 21m ago 13.07 EST 63 min: Arthur Clark is on for the captain, Luke Cowan-Dickie is back on from the sin-bin. England are pressuring the try-line of Japan again.
 Share 22m ago 13.06 EST 61 min: Joe Heyes, another new arrival, snatches the ball out of the air and looks to put England on the attack once again. Maro Itoje – who has had a fine, busy game – is soon to depart.
 Share 26m ago 13.02 EST 58 min: Steve Borthwick is starting to ring the changes. Marcus Smith is among the new entrants – Joseph has a chance to become the first England player to score his six tries in a game. If he doesn’t get brought off with an eye on the All Blacks to play next weekend.
 Share Updated at  13.02 EST 28m ago 13.00 EST TRY! England 61-15 Japan (Joseph)
 Will Joseph has a record-equalling five tries for England! That was all his own handiwork, he intercepted a Japan pass and just races through clear to touch down. Ford kicks the extras.
 Share 29m ago 12.58 EST YELLOW CARD! Cowan-Dickie (England)
 Luke Cowan-Dickie is in the sin-bin. Now it’s England who are down to 14 players – can Japan build on their impressive second half?
 Perhaps not …
 Share 32m ago 12.56 EST 53 min: Michael Stolberg almost breaks clear for Japan! He appeared in acres of space running for the line but his running is laboured and Pollock chases back to tackle him.
 Share 33m ago 12.54 EST 52 min: England on the attack once more – but Japan this time win the ball back and kick it clear. They look a bit more organised and/or fired up in this half.
 Share 35m ago 12.52 EST 50 min: England give away possession again and for the first time in the game you’d say Japan have a real spell of pressure. They’re in England’s half and searching for openings. But Itoje strips the ball in the tackle, finely done.
 Share 38m ago 12.50 EST 48 min: Archie McParland is on for his England debut, replacing Jack van Poortvliet! Can Archie get in on the attacking action?
 Share Updated at  12.53 EST 38m ago 12.49 EST TRY! England 54-15 Japan (Helu)
 Newcomer Opeti Helu gives England a taste of their own medicine! Japan get the ball moving quickly and the prop Helu powers over – the conversion misses.
 Share Updated at  12.51 EST 40m ago 12.47 EST 46 min: Japan change their hooker just before their own lineout. Huh. They’re inside their own half – is the Brave Blossom’s usually excellent lineout working at least? Yes, they collect.
 Share 41m ago 12.46 EST TRY! England 54-10 Japan (Martin)
 George Martin drives over – the fifth Beatle grabbing England’s ninth try! Too easy, really, he just battered his way through Japan’s defence from close range.
 View image in fullscreen George Martin goes over for yet another try. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA Share Updated at  13.23 EST 43m ago 12.44 EST 44 min: England power towards the try-line surely they will breakthrough again …
 Share 44m ago 12.43 EST 43 min: Japan lose possession, it’s been a scrappy start – but a laser-accurate kick from George Ford puts the visitors on the back foot.
 Share 46m ago 12.42 EST 41 min: Japan’s scrum – it collapses and they get a free-kick. Can Japan test England’s defence which didn’t look airtight the one time they were seriously tested in the first half?
 Share 47m ago 12.40 EST Second half
 England receive the ball to get us back under way! The hosts are unchanged.
 Share 48m ago 12.39 EST The teams are coming back out on to the pitch – Eddie Jones may have had a few things to say things to Japan about their defending.
 Share 52m ago 12.35 EST “Upset?” asks Gary Naylor (referring, I should say before you start worrying about his sanity, to Wales’s sublime display against the All Blacks rather than this game). “I’m no rugby expert, but is that the biggest single match upset in the sport? In all sport? Feels top 10 for sure.”
 It is gigantic. I know New Zealand had made some changes from the win in Scotland, but still. Nobody was predicting that.
 Michael Aylwin was in Cardiff to witness history if you want to read his report before the second half.
 Share 1h ago 12.31 EST “Ill-phrased, admittedly, but isn’t this a bit – well – pointless?” asks Andrew Sparrow by email. “The triumphalist TV commentary isn’t great either – we’re just kicking away a blind man’s stick.”
 It isn’t pretty for Japan. You can’t blame England’s players, of course – they all want and need to impress, win and entertain a packed stadium. But it was astonishingly one-sided.
 Share 1h ago 12.26 EST HALF-TIME: England 49-10 Japan
 Just the eight tries for the visitors – half of them by Will Joseph. Breathless stuff, Japan were overrun.
 View image in fullscreen Will Joseph dives to score England’s sixth try. Photograph: Matthew Lewis/Nations Championship/Getty Images Share Updated at  12.28 EST 1h ago 12.25 EST TRY! England 49-10 Japan (Earl)
 Maro Itoje leaps to catch the lineout , England drive for the line, Ben Earl gets the try. Simple stuff. Ford, this time, converts.
 Share 1h ago 12.23 EST 39 min: An England lineout near Japan’s try-line. Time for one more?
 Share 1h ago 12.22 EST TRY! England 42-10 Japan (Dearns)
 The 6ft 8in Warner Dearns forces his way under two England players to score Japan’s first try! The extras are kicked by Saito, too.
 View image in fullscreen Warner Dearns scores Japan's first try. Photograph: Matthew Lewis/Nations Championship/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.25 EST 1h ago 12.21 EST 35 min: Japan almost break through, Pollock stops them but the visitors aren’t done. They are exerting some pressure – and …
 Share 1h ago 12.19 EST 34 min: Japan win a lineout; one of their strengths. Some ball in hand now for the Brave Blossoms – they look to spread play.
 Share 1h ago 12.18 EST 33 min: Ellis Genge with a crunching tackle on Kanji Shimokawa. Jack van Poortvliet kicks a grubber though to Murley as England look to add to their try total – but it just has too much on it.
 Share 1h ago 12.16 EST 31 min: Japan finally get near the England try-line for the first time. Can their attack fare better than the visitor’s defence? Not quite, England win possession back and look to build.
